page: Amazon Web Services g5g.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton2 processors. The system delivers 64 physical cores across 64 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture clocked at 2.5 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by two bundled NVIDIA T4G GPUs from the Turing family, supplying a combined 32 GB of VRAM. The instance features a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a system optimized for parallel execution rather than per-thread intensity. Multi-core performance is robust, demonstrated by a stress-ng score of 97056.83, software compilation throughput of 42664.0 in Clang, and ray tracing benchmarks reaching 49128.0. Cached memory operations register high bandwidth at 3779.8 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput operations such as static web serving at 44.64 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 76.54 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded processing shows lower throughput, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and moderate compression speeds.

Hardware efficiency is grounded in the power efficiency of the Graviton2 processor paired with entry-tier NVIDIA T4G enterprise accelerators. For inference tasks, the configuration processes medium 7B parameter language models at 62.04 prompt tokens per second and 20.51 generation tokens per second, but degrades significantly on larger 70B models due to memory and compute bounds. The absence of local disk drives requires architectural planning around network I/O overhead.

The AWS g5g.16xlarge is aligned with parallelized Arm-native workloads requiring graphic or tensor acceleration, including Android cloud gaming, video rendering pipelines, computer vision inference, medium-scale machine learning model deployment, and distributed caching infrastructures.
